title: embeddings-rerank-incident-breadcrumbs-maya-patel-2026-03-07
content:
Breadcrumbs / scratchpad for the embeddings->rerank anomalies (dim mismatch + latency spikes)

Date: 2026-03-07
Owner: Maya Patel
Context: Customers reported rerank endpoint errors and intermittent latency spikes starting ~2026-03-05 08:30 UTC. Symptoms: 1) "dimension mismatch" errors in the rerank pipeline when merging query and doc embeddings; 2) p50/p95 latency jumps up to 2-3x baseline for short windows (~5-15 min).

Quick summary of hypothesis so far:
- Dimension mismatch likely due to model fallback/alias resolving to a different embedding model (512-d) instead of expected 1536-d model. Smart routing / fallback logic may have routed some requests to a smaller model during capacity constraints.
- Latency spikes correlate with Dedicated pool autoscaling events and occasional cold-starts on a small set of nodes (see grafana panel). Also a couple of high-CPU host traces while KV cache miss rate increased.

Things I tried (commands + outputs / notes)
1) Reproduce locally with curl against staging rerank endpoint (staging uses same routing logic):

$ curl -s -X POST "https://staging.api.redwood/v1/rerank" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query_embedding": [/* 1536 floats truncated */], "doc_embeddings": [[/* 1536 floats */], [/* 1536 floats */]] }' | jq .

Result: successful ranking response locally. No error when forcing correct dims.

2) Simulate a 512-d embedding being sent to rerank service (to validate error path):

$ python - <<PY
import requests, json
url = 'https://staging.api.redwood/v1/rerank'
headers={'Authorization':'Bearer REDACTED','Content-Type':'application/json'}
payload={'query_embedding':[0.0]*512,'doc_embeddings':[[0.0]*512]}
r=requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)
print(r.status_code, r.text[:500])
PY

Result: 400/422-ish response from service: "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but got 512" (exact snippet from logs below). Good: service rejects mismatch but need to understand how 512-d vectors entered pipeline.

3) Inspect model catalog and aliases during incident window (2026-03-05 08:30-09:00 UTC)

$ curl -s "https://platform.internal/v1/models" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${PLATFORM_TOKEN}" | jq '.models[] | {id,alias,dim}'

Observations: we have two embedding models in the pool:
- embed-large-1536 (id: embed-large-2026-02) dim=1536 alias: embed-search
- embed-small-512 (id: embed-small-2026-01) dim=512 alias: embed-search-fallback

Routing policy: alias 'embed-search' should map to embed-large-1536 for hosted customers; fallback/compatibility alias 'embed-search-fallback' available for low-memory nodes. Need to check if alias resolution logic accidentally returned the fallback alias name to the client or if smart routing returned a different model silently.

4) Check service logs for request ids flagged in support tickets. Example request id from ticket: rq_20260305_AB12

Kibana excerpt (trimmed):
2026-03-05T08:33:21Z rq_20260305_AB12 INFO rerank.handler Received request (model_alias=embed-search)
2026-03-05T08:33:21Z rq_20260305_AB12 DEBUG embeddings.fetcher resolved_model_id=embed-small-2026-01 (dim=512)
2026-03-05T08:33:21Z rq_20260305_AB12 ERROR rerank.pipeline embedding-dim-check failed expected=1536 got=512
2026-03-05T08:33:21Z rq_20260305_AB12 WARN routing.smart "fell back to embed-small-2026-01 due to capacity on pool dedicated-pool-3"

Conclusion from logs: routing did indeed fall back to embed-small-2026-01 for some requests and the fetcher returned 512-d vectors. The rerank pipeline's dim-check caught it and returned error. So root cause for dim mismatch = fallback to smaller model without converting or rejecting earlier.

5) Latency correlation: Grafana panels show p95 spikes at 08:32-08:37 UTC. Stacktrace/time-aligned events: autoscaler scaled up dedicated-pool-3 at 08:31:45, new nodes started with cold caches. KV cache miss rate increased from ~5% to ~68% during window. CPU on nodes with embed-large containers spiked while smart-routing redistributed requests.

Key log snippets (copied):
- "2026-03-05T08:31:46Z scale-controller INFO scaled up dedicated-pool-3 desired=8->10"
- "2026-03-05T08:32:02Z node-init INFO container embed-large-2026-02 started on node n-ctx-11"
- "2026-03-05T08:32:05Z router DEBUG routing decision: prefer=embed-large-2026-02 fallback=embed-small-2026-01 selected=fallback due to available_capacity<min_slo_capacity"

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) (High) Smart routing fallback is too permissive: it selects smaller-dim embedding model as a functional equivalent for 'embed-search' alias under capacity pressure. But rerank expects consistent dims and no on-the-fly projection is performed -> leads to dim mismatch errors.
2) (Medium) A recent change in alias resolution/compatibility matrix allowed fallback model to be returned with the same alias string, causing downstream components to assume dims are unchanged.
3) (Medium) Latency spikes are from autoscaling and cold-start cache misses; increased traffic on fewer nodes forced fallback decisions which then produced more errors (compounding).
4) (Low) A bug in client SDK that caches the model id and later sends requests with 512-d vectors, but this seems unlikely given server logs show resolved_model_id=embed-small-2026-01 at request time.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Rollback: temporary policy change to disable automatic fallback to embed-small-512 for the embed-search alias (feature flag) — flip applied at 09:10 UTC. Confirmed decrease in dim-mismatch errors after flag.
- Alerting: added temporary Grafana alert on embedding-dim-error rate > 0.1% and KV cache miss > 50% for 5m windows.

Longer-term fixes / action items:
- (ENG) Make routing aware of embedding-dimension compatibility: routing should never return a model with a different embedding dimension for the same alias unless a projection/conversion step is enabled and compatible. (owner: Jordan)
- (ENG) Add a runtime validation early in the request pipeline: verify embedding dims immediately after fetch and before merging; if mismatch, return 409 with structured error that includes resolved_model_id and request_id for triage. (owner: Maya)
- (ENG) Implement optional automatic projection path (512->1536) or standardized offline projection table, but only if quality tests pass. Add config flag to opt-in. (owner: Evelyn)
- (SRE) Investigate autoscaler thresholds: reduce oscillation and add warm-pool nodes for embed-large model type to avoid cold-starts during spikes. (owner: SRE oncall)
- (DX) Update SDK docs to clearly state embedding dims per model alias and warn about mixing dims. (owner: docs)

Open questions:
- How did routing pick fallback for some customers but not others? Is it per-customer capacity gating or global? Need to inspect routing policy logs in more detail for customer ids.
- Should we add a transform layer that pads/embeds 512->1536 automatically? That has quality risks.
- Did any downstream consumers silently store 512-d vectors assuming 1536? Need to scan DBs (vector stores) for embedding shape anomalies.

Next immediate steps (today):
- Jordan: add dimension-check early in staging and add unit tests around alias->model resolution matrix (ETA EOD).
- Evelyn: run a quick search for saved embeddings in vector-store snapshots 2026-03-05..2026-03-06 and report any 512-length vectors (ETA tomorrow morning).
- Maya (me): post incident summary to #embeddings and update JIRA INC-1427 with mitigation steps and links to logs/dashboards (ETA 11:00).

Notes to self / debugging crumbs:
- Req ids with errors: rq_20260305_AB12, rq_20260305_CD34, rq_20260305_EF99 (see Kibana filter for request_id:rq_20260305_*)
- Check router service mem/threads at 08:30 window (we saw a few "routing queue full" WARNs)
- Watch for any SDK changes in the last 2 weeks that touch model alias caching (PRs: repo/sdk PR#200, PR#204).

Appendix: raw error snippet captured from rerank service logs

"2026-03-05T08:33:21Z rq_20260305_AB12 ERROR rerank.pipeline: embedding-dim-check failed - expected=1536 got=512 - resolved_model_id=embed-small-2026-01 - user_id=acct_34f2 - route=prod/rerank-v2"
"Trace: rerank.pipeline.merge_embeddings -> rerank.pipeline.validate_dims -> ValueError('Embedding dim mismatch: expected 1536 got 512')"

End of notes. Will iterate after Jordan and Evelyn findings.
